slides.title: What an IIS Actually Is
bullets: Investigator or institution designs, leads, and sponsors the study
Company may fund it or supply study medication, or both
Full scientific and editorial control stays with the investigator
One of the most valuable evidence sources for Medical Affairs

slides.title: Interface, Guide, and Relationship Manager
bullets: MSL bridges field science and the company's internal evidence agenda
Identifies a genuine investigator interest in a research question
Recognizes whether it fills a real, uncovered evidence need
Helps the investigator navigate the formal IIS submission process
Carries field learning back to internal evidence and strategy teams

slides.title: The Ethical Lines an MSL Cannot Cross
bullets: Can explain process, eligibility, and submission timelines
Cannot influence the study's scientific design
Cannot make support conditional on favorable results
Cannot factor in commercial decisions about prescriber-investigators

slides.title: From Request to Decision
bullets: Investigator submits a formal IIS request
An internal committee, separate from commercial, reviews it
Reviewers assess scientific relevance and methodological feasibility
Alignment with company evidence priorities is also weighed
Approval or denial follows documented, auditable criteria

slides.title: Real Contribution, Preserved Independence
bullets: Supporting IIS well is one of an MSL's most tangible contributions
Connects genuine clinical questions to company funding and product
Investigator independence is what gives the study its credibility

takeaway.title: IIS studies convert genuine investigator questions into credible evidence, with the MSL as facilitator, not scientific director
bullets: MSL guides process without touching scientific design or outcomes
Ethical separation from commercial protects the study's credibility
Independent review committees decide approval, not the MSL relationship
